data.why: The app ships its own samples/ directory served via Vite's virtual:samples plugin and the Files tab's bundled 'samples' folder; these are also handed to the browser as direct upload/open test files covering a CFX .zpcr run, its encrypted .pcrd counterpart, another .zpcr qualification run, a Biomeme melt run, and a .plt.csv plate definition.

goals: Open a .zpcr run export and inspect amplification curves per well and channel
Switch the curve view between Raw and ΔRFU baselining, and Linear and Log scale
Review the thermal protocol and run timing, including whether the run completed or stopped short
Inspect melt curves and the derived Tm for a run or a Biomeme export
Compare the .pcrd file's CFX-reported Cq against the app's own computed Cq per well
Browse the raw archive contents (hex/ASCII/XML) of a .zpcr/.pcrd file for a given entry

review.summary: The tree covers what scientists mainly do with this qPCR file viewer: amplification curves with baseline/scale/threshold, the melt Tm table, protocol vs as-run timing, optical reference drift, and the raw archive. Every screen I sampled matches its node. It needs fixes before filing: two stated goals are missing (run completeness, and file vs computed Cq via the Biomeme toggle that was available), t12 is session-specific, plate editing is filed under optics, and the Calibration and Overview components have no features.
